matches.title: Expanding TDS' Economy
matches.snippet: Expanding TDS' Economy Introduction TDS only has three economy towers, and one of them is just a downgraded version of another - it won't even be considered here. The Golden Cowboy and Farm have had a varied place in the meta over time, whether it be amidst countless rebalances or none at all. These towers allow you to spend money to get more money in return - it's hard for them to be 'bad' towers due to this simple positive loop. Despite this simplicity, there are only two economy towers in the game - I'm surprised we don't have more, with unique mechanics stacked onto them - currently we only have a tower that generates cash and a tower that shoots and generates cash. Yes, adding new economy towers would likely be a balancing nightmare, as shown by the current two we already have, but it would help make the game more interesting, I'd reckon. This hypothetical suggests that economy towers be the norm and get more focus, and more towers filling the role. Naturally, a few other things need to be changed before this can be done. Sniper: Bad tower overall because of mid damage and high fire rate, but it IS cheap fly detection, so if you're poor and need help against those Balloon Kids, this will work. Just be sure to upgrade it. Paintballer: Usually, paintball guns aren't really useful in the apocalypse and this is true for this too. I can only see its use in Easy Mode as a cheap early game option, but good luck using this to beat harder gamemodes. At least it has lead, even though the weak paintballs can't kill them, especially when they're in swarms. NO HD, NO FLY, THIS IS ABSOLUTE GARBAGE. Demoman: The aiming gimmick gives it a bit of a sledger situation, where quick enemies can dodge its attacks. Luckily the higher upgrades remove this. Pretty good splash damage tower, but HD is still a problem because it's locked away at max level. Hunter: Basically a sniper on the ground. No point in using it though because the ground is usually where higher DPS towers are placed, and it sorta just wastes space for those towers. However, it is a pretty good fly-detection tower and when spammed, it destroys swarms of weak enemies. Soldier: Really good tower for early game because of its high burst of damage. It can solo Easy Mode on Crossroads/Rocket Arena and overall is the best Starter tower. But in late game, the soldier quickly becomes useless as higher-health enemies come in. INTERMEDIATE TOWERS Militant: With support towers, some farms to get the upgrades quick, and an early-game defender, the Militant can beat Molten Mode on most maps. Its a more spammable, alternative version to the Minigunner, and overall is really good. It also has fly detection and hidden detection, so its high damage output and spammability can make it a good early-game hardcore tower, taking down even a mega slow when enough are placed down. Medic: Underrated. The Medic, being bad at easier gamemodes, is ESSENTIAL for harder ones, where you're getting stunned left, right and center. The stun cleansing allows for quick recovery and maximizes damage dealt to the boss, and with your steady stream of cash, level 5 medics will not be a problem to spam. Freezer: Ever since the rework, the Freezer is just a scout/soldier that slows down enemies. Pretty decent option when you need to slow enemies, but honestly just get an electroshocker. Farm: What more can I say? It's the farm. Its a great option that provides HEAVY doses of cash at the end of the wave, allowing you to get stronger towers quicker. Essential for your game. Shotgunner: When you need to speed past the early rounds, shotgunner is here! The shotgunner is a spammable tower that honestly acts more like a melee option, meaning that it has low range and high damage. Using this on a map like Crossroads or Rocket Arena on Easy/Molten/Intermediate allows you to SPEED past the early game. Sometimes the boss health bars even flash red when it shoots. However, after each enemy debut, the shotgunner slowly and slowly becomes less useful in your run, so you should probably sell them later on. Rocketeer: The hunter version of the Mortar, the Rocketeer offers high damage with splash at a slow fire rate. Its decent, but the deadzone can be a problem even if you place it far from the path. I don't see myself using this. Trapper: Can help you catch leaks from weak enemies, but you really must be a master of placement to make this work. Late game enemies also are super strong and can probably just plow through the traps, so be careful when using it. Super bad on tracks with multiple lanes. Ace Pilot: The main use for this is hardcore, but I do see it being used in maps such as Pizza Party to counter Balloon Kids. However it's generally better to bring other towers with higher DPS to your game, but this is a good tower. You can also place it near your rangers to give them HD for a while, and using this strat I soloed Molten on Wrecked. Pyromancer: good for EARLY EARLY game and against invisibles when level 2, but the fact that i cant be bothered to even have correct grammar definitely says something. defense melting can be useful though. Military Base: Solid tower with many upsides. It can also clutch your run when some unit spawns when you're about to lose. Absolute chad tower, but be sure to get Mounted Gunners as soon as possible. Crook Boss: This tower is just Military Base but the tower itself shoots at enemies. The goons the Crook Boss summons stop walking when shooting, so they can stack up to deal massive damage, but I don't use it enough to be talking. ADVANCED TOWERS Electroshocker: High damage along with stuns make this tower really good. However a LOT of zombies have stun immunity, so it has a sort-of shotgunner situation, where it becomes worse with every wave passed.
